cls: Topical anti-inflammatory / anti-allergic agent (aphthous ulcer therapy)
pharm: A synthetic anti-inflammatory, anti-allergic compound applied as a 5% oral paste to aphthous ulcers (canker sores); it inhibits the formation and/or release of inflammatory mediators (such as histamine and leukotrienes) from mast cells, neutrophils, and mononuclear cells, accelerating ulcer healing and reducing pain.
quick: 5% paste: apply ~0.5 cm (1/4 inch) to each ulcer 4 times daily
Apply after oral hygiene following meals and at bedtime
Use only if clearly needed; limited data
Ulcer healing; local irritation or contact reaction
summary: Amlexanox is a topical anti-inflammatory and anti-allergic agent formulated as a 5% oral paste for the treatment of aphthous ulcers (canker sores) in patients with normal immune systems. Applied directly to each ulcer four times daily - after oral hygiene following meals and at bedtime - it speeds healing and reduces pain, with benefit usually seen within a few days; healing is typically faster than with no treatment. Its precise mechanism is not fully defined but it inhibits the formation/release of inflammatory and allergic mediators such as histamine and leukotrienes. It is for topical oral use only. Patients should wash their hands after application and discontinue if a rash or contact mucositis develops. If significant healing or pain relief has not occurred in about 10 days, they should be re-evaluated.
indications: Treatment of aphthous ulcers (canker sores) in immunocompetent patients

dosage.d: Apply approximately 0.5 cm (1/4 inch) of paste directly onto each ulcer four times daily
dosage.t: Four times daily (after meals and at bedtime)
dosage.n: Start as soon as symptoms appear; continue until the ulcer heals, then stop

admin: For topical use in the mouth only; do not swallow the paste
Apply after oral hygiene following meals and at bedtime, four times a day
Squeeze about 0.5 cm (1/4 inch) of paste onto a fingertip and dab it gently and directly onto each mouth ulcer
Wash hands immediately before and after each application
Begin treatment as soon as the first symptoms of a canker sore appear, and re-evaluate if no meaningful healing occurs within about 10 days
moa: Amlexanox is an anti-inflammatory and anti-allergic agent. Although the exact mechanism by which it heals aphthous ulcers is unknown, it has been shown to inhibit the formation and/or release of inflammatory mediators - including histamine and leukotrienes - from activated mast cells, neutrophils, and mononuclear cells. By dampening this local inflammatory and allergic response in the oral mucosa, it reduces inflammation and pain and accelerates the resolution of canker sores. Applied topically, systemic exposure is low.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to amlexanox or any component of the paste
relative: Development of a rash or contact mucositis with use
monitor: Healing and pain of the aphthous ulcer
Local irritation, rash, or contact mucositis
Lack of response after about 10 days (re-evaluate)

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; animal studies have not shown major adverse effects at exposures relevant to topical dosing. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and the benefit justifies the risk.
lact: It is not known whether amlexanox is excreted in human milk after topical oral use; systemic exposure is low. Exercise caution when used by a nursing mother.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is required for topical oral use because systemic absorption is limited.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is required for topical oral use because systemic absorption is limited.

minor: No clinically significant drug interactions have been established for the topical oral paste given its limited systemic absorption
interactions.food: Apply after eating and oral hygiene; the paste itself is used in the mouth and not taken with food.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference described.

common: Transient stinging, burning, or pain at the application site
emergency: Severe allergic reaction with swelling of the lips/tongue/throat or difficulty breathing (rare)

monitoring: Healing of the aphthous ulcer (typically improvement within days)
Local irritation, rash, or contact mucositis
Response by about day 10 - re-evaluate if not healing
counsel: Use this paste only in your mouth on the canker sores - do not swallow it
Wash your hands before and after applying it
Dab a small amount (about a quarter inch) directly on each sore four times a day, after meals and at bedtime
Start as soon as you feel a canker sore beginning for the best effect
A brief stinging or burning when you apply it is normal
Stop and contact your dentist or doctor if you get a rash or mouth irritation, or if the sore is not healing after about 10 days
pk: Symptom relief and faster healing typically over a few days
Acts locally at the ulcer site; low systemic levels
Applied four times daily until the ulcer heals
Store at controlled room temperature ~20-25 C; keep the tube tightly closed
pearls: FDA-approved (originally as Aphthasol 5% oral paste) for aphthous ulcers in immunocompetent patients - note it may be absent from openFDA structured data
Start at the first sign of a canker sore and apply four times daily; healing is faster than with no treatment
Mechanism is inhibition of inflammatory/allergic mediator release (histamine, leukotrienes) from mast cells and leukocytes
Topical oral use only - wash hands before and after, do not swallow
Re-evaluate if the ulcer has not meaningfully healed in about 10 days (consider other causes)
Stop if rash or contact mucositis develops
missed: If you miss an application, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next application, skip the missed one and continue your regular four-times-daily schedule - do not apply extra paste to make up for it.
overdose: Overdose with the topical oral paste is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity because absorption is low. If a large amount is accidentally swallowed, manage supportively; there is no specific antidote.
